title: Improving and Accelerating Offline RL in Large Discrete Action Spaces with Structured Policy Initialization
claim: Our method reaches target performance almost immediately after a short pre-training phase, while baselines need hours of training to get there.
layout: 1 panel, line plot, time on x-axis, dashed target and pre-training lines
description: A single line chart of wall-clock time in minutes (x-axis, 0 to 300) against percent of FIQL asymptotic score (y-axis, 0 to about 115). The SPIN curve is thick and dark navy. It stays at zero until a thin dashed vertical line at about 9 minutes, labeled 'ASM Learning Complete', then jumps vertically to about 100%. It keeps climbing to about 113% and stays there. Three thinner baseline curves, Factored IQL (blue), SAINT (red) and AR-IQL (cyan), rise gradually and only approach or cross the dashed horizontal 100% line after roughly 150 to 200 minutes. SAINT ends highest of the three, near 109%. A legend sits in the lower right. The eye goes first to the steep navy jump and the gap above the baselines.
caption: In the humanoid-stand task, learning from the medium-expert dataset, SPIN reaches the target performance (dashed horizontal line) quickly after pre-training (dashed vertical line), while baselines require over 200 minutes of wall-clock training.
abstract: Reinforcement learning in discrete combinatorial action spaces requires searching over exponentially many joint actions to simultaneously select multiple sub-actions that form coherent combinations. Existing approaches either simplify policy learning by assuming independence across sub-actions, which often yields incoherent or invalid actions, or attempt to learn action structure and control jointly, which is slow and unstable. We introduce Structured Policy Initialization (SPIN), a two-stage framework that first pre-trains an Action Structure Model (ASM) to capture the manifold of valid actions, then freezes this representation and trains lightweight policy heads for control. On challenging discrete DM Control benchmarks, SPIN improves average return by up to 39% over the state of the art while reducing time to convergence by up to 12.8$\times$.
